chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'All showing-off is shirk. Indeed, whoever does a deed for the people, his reward is upon the people, and whoever does a deed for Allah, his reward is upon Allah.'

key_terms.ثَوَابُهُ: His reward; the spiritual recompense for a deed
key_terms.رِيَاءٍ: Showing-off; performing deeds to be seen by people
key_terms.شِرْكٌ: Shirk; associating partners with God or giving share to others in worship/intention
key_terms.لِلنَّاسِ: For the people; done for the sake of human approval or recognition

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between showing-off (riya') and shirk in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes riya' (showing-off) as a subtle form of shirk by contrasting the recipients of reward: deeds done for people yield their reward from people, while those done for God are retained by Him. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ikhlas (sincerity) as the essential condition for the acceptance of worship, linking the internal state of the heart directly to the metaphysical outcome of the deed.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra’a, from Yazeed Bin Khaleefa who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Showing-off is Shirk (association with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>). The one who does a deed for the people, his rewards would be upon the people, and the one who does a deed for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, his Reward would be upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al- Mighra’ from Yazid ibn Khalifah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Showing off is considering things as partners of Allah. Whoever works for people, his rewards are upon the people and whoever works for Allah, his reward is before Allah.’”
